evidence.claim: An 1810 state highway act incorporated an existing road between Westport and Saranac Lake through Keene.
evidence.quote: On April 5, 1810, the New York State Legislature passed an act establishing a new state highway linking Westport to Hopkinton by way of Keene and Saranac Lake. The highway incorporated the entirety of the pre-existing roadway between Westport and Saranac Lake.

evidence.claim: In 1816 it appointed commissioners to rebuild from opposite ends and meet midway. Work finished by 1818 on the North West Bay Road.
evidence.quote: On April 17, 1816, the state attempted to correct the issue by approving a measure that appointed two sets of commissioners to oversee the reconstruction of the highway. Each set was to work on opposite ends of the route and eventually converge at a point midway along the route. Work on the highway was completed by 1818.

evidence.claim: The Lake Placid Club’s first jump here used the hillside itself as a takeoff surface in 1920.
evidence.quote: The Lake Placid Club built the first ski jump on this site in 1920, using the hillside itself as the jump surface.

evidence.claim: A steel tower followed in 1927 and was raised in 1928 for the jump later used at the 1932 Winter Olympics.
evidence.quote: in 1927, a new steel tower was built, raising the jump to 60 meters. In 1928, the tower was raised to 75 meters; this was the tower used for the 1932 Winter Olympic Games.

evidence.claim: That tower was demolished in 1977 to make way for two new jumps for the 1980 Games.
evidence.quote: In 1977, the old tower was demolished to make way for new 70 and 90-meter jumps, used for the 1980 Winter Olympic Games.

evidence.claim: The concrete towers were poured continuously using a jacking system: fifteen days for the larger tower, nine for the smaller.
evidence.quote: The towers were built using a jacking system that lifted and poured concrete into the forms continuously, night and day, for 15 days for the larger jump, and 9 days for the smaller one.

evidence.claim: A gondola replaced the aging double chairlift serving the ski jumps in 2019.
evidence.quote: In 2019, a pulse gondola was installed to replace an aging double chair which served the ski jumps.

evidence.claim: Both jumps received further upgrades for year-round training in 2021.
evidence.quote: In 2021, both jumps received upgrades that enabled year-round training and increased reliability

evidence.claim: The Cascade Lakes began as one body of water, Long Pond, beneath a mountain then called Long Pond Mountain.
evidence.quote: Prior to 1860, the mountain was named "Long Pond Mountain" for a pond located at its base. Long Pond was divided by a landslide shortly after 1860

evidence.claim: A landslide shortly after 1860 split the pond in two.
evidence.quote: Long Pond was divided by a landslide shortly after 1860

evidence.claim: The divided waters were called Edmund’s Ponds until 1878, when Sidney and Warren Weston built a hotel between them.
evidence.quote: the divided ponds were named "Edmund's Ponds" until 1878, when Sidney and Warren Weston built a hotel in between the two ponds.

evidence.claim: The Westons renamed them Cascade Lakes for the waterfall flowing down the landslide’s path; the mountain took the Cascade name as well.
evidence.quote: They renamed the ponds the "Cascade Lakes", after a waterfall flowing down the mountain in the path of the landslide, and Long Pond Mountain was renamed to Cascade Mountain.
